title: Park death prompts Taser call; Three officers identified in shooting Victim mourned at Scarborough home: [ONT Edition]
article: The man fatally shot by police Sunday might be alive today if Toronto officers were equipped with stun guns, Ontario's community safety minister says.

"Tasers are guns that send out an electrical current that would in fact incapacitate somebody like that," Monte Kwinter told reporters at Queen's Park yesterday. "It's unfortunate that the particular officers that were there were not equipped with Tasers, (because) that would have without question resulted in a different outcome."
But Kwinter said it is up to each police force to determine whether they should buy the non-lethal weapons.
O'brien Christopher\-Reid, 26, was shot after he allegedly lunged at three police officers with a knife.

The province's special investigations unit, which is investigating the case, would not reveal the names of the officers. But a source identified them as Constable Rick Milsom, Constable John Leggio and Sergeant Darren Berezowski.
Milsom was in the news 20 years ago, when he shot and wounded a robber outside a Scarborough branch of Canada Trust.

An autopsy was performed yesterday on Christopher-Reid, but SIU spokesperson Kaia Werbus said the results will not be immediately released to the public. The SIU is continuing its investigation, Werbus said.

Friends and family of the dead man gathered last night to mourn his death. Outside a detached yellow brick two-storey home in Scarborough, three women waited to offer their condolences. They hugged and bent their heads as if in prayer. As the evening progressed, a stream of friends and neighbours came to comfort the family.
"We are seeking legal counsel," said Rockell King, a cousin of the deceased and a spokesperson for the family. "My cousin O'brien Christopher\-Reid was a very loving young man."

"His mother and his father, his brother, sister - our entire family - is absolutely shocked and completely devastated by the events of the last 24 hours. We feel we are missing lots of information. There isn't much more I can say at this point."

Officers continued to comb the park yesterday, taking pictures and looking for witnesses. Yellow police tape sealed off the entrance to the walking trails inside the park. Three police officers are the subject of the inquiry, with six other officers being questioned as witnesses, Werbus said.

"We have spoken to five out of the six witness officers, but we're still looking for other witnesses," said Werbus. The tragic events began around noon Sunday, when members of the Toronto police responded to a 911 call. There had been reports of a man carrying a knife along Lawrence Ave. E., heading for Edwards Gardens.

Three officers searched for the man and, according to sources and witnesses, when they caught up with him in Wilket Creek Park he was swinging an electrical cord in one hand, and the officers tried to calm him down.
According to sources, the man started to run and the officers followed. He allegedly lunged at them with a knife when they caught him. All three officers fired, sources said.

The suspect didn't say anything to the police as they surrounded him other than telling them "I'm going to kill you," a source said. When he lunged at one of the officers with a 25-centimetre knife, the source said, he came within 50 centimetres of striking one of them and that's when the shots were fired by police.

About eight shots in total were fired from the three police- issued Glocks before the suspect fell, according to the source. One officer fired more than the others, but determining which bullets came from which guns will be difficult for forensic experts because the type of rounds used by police aren't easily traceable, the source said.
In the melee, Constable Milsom was shot and wounded in the leg, the source said. He was treated and released from Sunnybrook hospital. Police are still investigating how the officer was shot.

The SIU is also seeking Salima Hadibhai and Shakeel Ladha, who were having engagement pictures taken in the park on Sunday. The couple told the Star they saw a man enter the park who was shirtless, his pants falling off his hips, and visibly upset and muttering. Investigators are also interested in talking to Zahir Hirji, their photographer.

In March, 1984, Milsom was flagged down by a Canada Trust branch manager who said a man had just threatened tellers and fled with about $3,100. Milson caught the suspect as he was getting into a getaway car.
The robber was armed with a replica weapon and pointed the gun at Milsom. He was ordered to put the gun down and when he refused, Milson fired three times, hitting him once in the buttocks.
